text:
Mistake we see a lot: booking a "twin" in Tokyo to get more floor space. On the plan we read, the twin was 4.6 m² bigger, and the second bed took most of it 👇

🤔 A or B? Pick one, then see what we found 👉 https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-double-or-twin-two-suitcases

❌ THE MISTAKE

🛏️ Paying ¥4,400 more for the twin at the same Ueno hotel (¥19,650 vs ¥15,250 for the double, Wed 16 Dec 2026, 2 adults).

📐 The official plan shows two 120 cm beds pushed side by side, and one strip of floor about 95 cm wide at their foot.

✅ THE FIX

1️⃣ Look for the hotel's own floor plan, not just "m²". Where is the free floor, and how wide is it?

2️⃣ Compare a bigger double. At the same hotel the deluxe double was about 18 m² with one 180 cm bed, for ¥18,750, less than the twin. Ask for a photo first, because that plan is not published.

3️⃣ Price one area farther out. A 25 m² flat in Kinshicho was ¥10,968 the same night, with no longer ride to Shinjuku or Shibuya.

4️⃣ Check the check-in hours. That flat opens its door at 16:00, which matters if you land in the morning.

👉 The plans and the full comparison:
https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-double-or-twin-two-suitcases

Save this for when you book your Tokyo room 📌
